method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Meniere's disease: intratympanic therapy, low-salt diet, surgical options
topic.coverageNote: Covers sodium restriction, intratympanic steroid, endolymphatic surgery, and destructive surgery for Ménière disease. A stored BPPV document was not used.

mcqs.question: What does this review say about dietary sodium restriction?

options.A: It has been widely used since 1931, but controlled studies using modern definitions are lacking, and some advocate moderate rather than harsh restriction
options.B: A randomised trial in this paper proves harsh restriction stops all spells
options.D: It was introduced after gentamicin and is first-line destructive therapy
options.E: The review does not discuss diet

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It has been widely used since 1931, but controlled studies using modern definitions are lacking, and some advocate moderate rather than harsh restriction
mcqs.explanation: Sodium restriction has been widely used since 1931. Reduction of dietary sodium plus diuretics has been reported to slow hearing-loss progression. Some advocate moderate regulation rather than harsh restriction, and controlled studies using modern definitions are lacking.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Sodium restriction This has been widely used to control symptoms of Ménière’s disease since 1931.

mcqs.question: Which diuretic combination does the review call the most commonly used medical treatment?

options.B: Spironolactone as the only diuretic ever used
options.C: Acetazolamide is the only agent with a licence for Ménière disease

mcqs.explanation: A combination of hydrochlorothiazide and triamterene is the most commonly used medical treatment. Acetazolamide, furosemide, and spironolactone are also used by some.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A combination of hydrochlorothiazide and triamterene is the most commonly used medical treatment for Ménière’s disease.

mcqs.question: What effect does the review attribute to intratympanic steroids?

options.A: A calming effect, with fewer and less severe spells for up to 2 years
options.B: Immediate recovery of hearing to normal in all patients
options.C: They are useful in migraine but not in Ménière disease
options.D: They ablate vestibular function like gentamicin

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A calming effect, with fewer and less severe spells for up to 2 years
mcqs.explanation: Intratympanic steroids have been noted to have a calming effect on Ménière ears. The number and severity of spells seem to decrease for up to 2 years.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Intratympanic steroids have been noted to have a calming effect on Ménière’s ears. 24 The number and severity of spells seem to decrease for up to 2 years after use.

mcqs.question: What vertigo-control result does the review cite for endolymphatic shunts and sac procedures?

options.A: Improvement in about two-thirds, similar to improvement in nonsurgical cases over time
options.C: Worse vertigo than the natural history in every series
options.D: These operations are no longer described

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Improvement in about two-thirds, similar to improvement in nonsurgical cases over time
mcqs.explanation: Endolymphatic shunts, cochleosacculotomy, and sac decompression have been used for decades. Vertigo control improved in about two-thirds, similar to nonsurgical cases over time.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Improvement in vertigo control has been achieved in about two-thirds of treated patients. 29 This is similar to the improvement seen in nonsurgically treated cases over time.

mcqs.question: Which destructive options does the review name when the aim is to disconnect a failing labyrinth, and when are they usually avoided?

options.A: Gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy; usually avoided when disease is bilateral
options.B: Endolymphatic shunt as the only destructive operation
options.D: Sodium restriction is the destructive step
options.E: They are preferred in bilateral disease

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy; usually avoided when disease is bilateral
mcqs.explanation: The favoured destructive means named are gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy. Destructive procedures are not usually used in bilateral cases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the favored means are destructive: gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy. The rationale for these treatments is to functionally disconnect the labyrinth
